title: Index librorum theutonicorum impressorum & manuscriptorum Romae anno 1806 ... BSB Cbm Cat. 557
shelf_note: A handwritten 1806 shelf-list of German books in the Vatican library: a bibliographic tool, not a primary source of any tradition we shelve. No tradition and no collection are set. It is useful as provenance reference, but it is off-mission as reading matter.
structure_note: 456/458 pages have OCR and 451 are translated; nothing odd in the counts. The three sampled pages carry the hand's folio numbers 56, 113 and an unnumbered one, consistent with order. The key data on every page is the right-hand shelf number ('Pro'), and the OCR gets it wrong on whole pages (see p.229).

ocr_errors.problem: 'et postea ad' fused into a non-word

tr_errors.english: on the German Empire devolved to the Saxon Franks
tr_errors.problem: the title says the Empire passed to the Franks and afterwards to the Saxons; the translation merges the two peoples into one, which is a different claim
the OCR misreading is carried into an invented English name

other.note: The <summary> calls this 'This final page', but it is folio 56 of a ~450-page list.

ocr_errors.problem: every Vatican shelf number on the page is misread (13xx read as 15xx), and these numbers are the point of the index
'papistical' read as 'peaceful', which reverses the polemic
year misread
a deleted word is transcribed as text

tr_errors.problem: Osiander's tract was against 34 'papist' articles; the reader is told the opposite

ocr_errors.problem: 'De' inserted

book_verdict: The pages are right and the prose of the entries is mostly legible. But on p.229 the OCR misreads every shelf number (1390→1590 …) and turns 'papisticos' into 'pacificos', so the index's one job — locating a book — fails. It is also a doubtful fit for the shelves.

title: Pedanii Dioscoridis De Medica Materia Libri Quinque (1546)
shelf_note: Ruel's Latin Dioscorides (Cologne 1546) is a core early-modern materia medica; it fits europeanlibraries and early science.
structure_note: 712 pages, all OCR'd and translated. The printed page numbers (149, 327, 504) track the image index at a steady offset of 30. Nothing stands out.

ocr_errors.problem: side-note dropped

tr_errors.english: it covers the bare glans of the uncircumcised
tr_errors.problem: 'recutiti' are the circumcised; the translation inverts it, though the next clause partly repairs the sense

tr_errors.english: assists against the bites of spiders
tr_errors.problem: mus araneus is the shrew-mouse, not a spider

tr_errors.source: Cui, antequàm aliquid ex ijs accidat, vomitus & aqua mulsa prod [page ends]
tr_errors.english: ...vomiting and honey-water will be of help: afterwards, natron and wormwood should be taken with sweet wine ... rose oil and vinegar ... eupatorium ... the odor from the extinguishing of lamps ... stir up sneezing
tr_errors.problem: Five sentences of mandrake treatment that are not on this leaf are appended after the catchword. This is lookahead from the next page, presented as this page's text.

other.note: The <summary> mentions 'the Sardonia herb', which is not named on the page (only 'Sardonio risu').

book_verdict: The transcription is clean and the translation is fluent and mostly faithful. One page carries a translated passage from the next leaf (T5), and there are two moderate lexical slips (spiders for shrews, uncircumcised for circumcised).

title: Conpotus (sic) magistri Roperti anglici linconiensis episcopi
shelf_note: Grosseteste's Computus, a 13th-c. Harvard manuscript: medieval science (calendar and lunar astronomy). It fits the early-science orbit, though no tradition or collection is set.
structure_note: Of 62 pages, 61 have OCR and 49 are translated. The pencil foliation on p.43 ('19') matches the OCR page-num. Nothing broken; the problem is the reading of the abbreviated Gothic hand.

ocr_errors.ocr: poenitentes. no intellige paschales eidem anni
ocr_errors.image: p[ro]concurrentes. no[n] intellige p[ro]currentes eidem anni s[ed] sequentis anni
ocr_errors.problem: 'concurrentes' (a technical computus term) is read as 'penitents', 'paschales', 'excelsenau' and 'excelsent' across the page; the abbreviations are not expanded and become non-words

ocr_errors.ocr: Inapit autem cyclus iste ad ianuario. et amarao
ocr_errors.image: Incipit autem cyclus iste no[n] a ianuario s[ed] a martio
ocr_errors.problem: the negation is lost: the cycle begins NOT in January BUT in March

ocr_errors.ocr: regulare illi mensis ... reglaru iuny ē G.
ocr_errors.problem: letters and numerals of the regulars misread

tr_errors.source: Inapit autem cyclus iste ad ianuario. et amarao
tr_errors.english: This cycle begins at January, and amarao <gloss>bitterness/bitter</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: the sense is reversed (the source says it begins in March, not January), and 'a martio' is glossed as 'bitterness'

tr_errors.source: excelsenau, phos scirenau, tapiao, lige, ferraze …
tr_errors.problem: OCR non-words are given confident invented glosses; the 'translation' is word salad with no uncertainty marked

ocr_errors.ocr: fin autem dielem ignota est uni sedi
ocr_errors.problem: the name of the authority (Arzachel / al-Zarqali) is lost
the key number (excess of the 19-year cycle) is misread, twice
the Calippic 76-year / 940-lunation period becomes 16 and 20
an abbreviation is rendered as a non-word throughout

tr_errors.source: 6939 dies et insuper 16. minuta ... 16. anni ... 20. luner
tr_errors.english: 6939 days and in addition 16 minutes ... 16 years ... 20 of the moon
tr_errors.problem: the wrong figures are carried into a fluent but meaningless argument; 'spleene' becomes 'the moon'

ocr_errors.problem: numeral misread; 'et' read as '7'
the opening word of the sentence becomes a non-word
'saltus lunae' (the moon's leap), the central computus term, is lost

tr_errors.source: in qua in die talis lune
tr_errors.english: in which in the day of such moon
tr_errors.problem: the saltus lunae is lost, so the passage's point is lost; the rest is a literal word-by-word rendering of garble ('7th night 3', 'impeded place')

book_verdict: A valuable 13th-c. computus manuscript, but the OCR does not resolve its abbreviations. It produces non-words and wrong numerals (16 for 44 minutes, 16/20 for 76 years/940 lunations), and the translation dresses them in confident invented glosses. An expert would not trust a line of it.

title: Lexicon alchemiae
shelf_note: Faust's 1727 alchemical lexicon and its companion treatise: squarely alchemy.
structure_note: The record holds more than the Lexicon. Pages 202 and 304 carry the running head 'De vera & natur. scientia &c.' (printed pp. 65 and 153), a separate German-Latin treatise bound in or issued with it. The title and language ('Latin') describe only the first part (I7). eligible_pages (394) exceeds pages_count (378), which suggests split/crop records, but the sampled leaves are right.

ocr_errors.problem: small slip

tr_errors.english: ...; a deep soaking or sinking into a substance.
tr_errors.problem: editorial expansions added to the definitions without marking

other.note: The leading <meta> asserts what the previous page ended with ('Pater ante filium'), which cannot be checked from this leaf.

book_verdict: Clean OCR and good, heavily annotated translations; showable. The catalogue should say the volume also contains the German-Latin 'De vera & naturali scientia' treatise.

title: Ars artium sive Ars magna cabalistica (PH337)
shelf_note: A manuscript kabbalistic-arithmetic treatise (BPH): Kabbalah shelf.
structure_note: Of 192 pages, 190 are OCR'd and 178 translated. The catalogue date 1566 does not match the copy: p.95 cites 'Esch Mezareph' (published in Knorr's Kabbala Denudata, 1677–84), so this hand is later than 1566. The date probably belongs to the work, not the witness (I7, moderate). Hand page numbers 44, 9, 54 against image indices 50, 95, 140 suggest separately paginated sections, not a defect.

ocr_errors.problem: signature invented, catchword dropped

ocr_errors.image: the edge of the facing page's text
ocr_errors.problem: the neighbouring leaf's text is transcribed as a margin of this page

other.note: The translation has broken markup: an empty '<margin></margin>' followed by a stray '</margin>' after the <unclear> fragments.

the worked check is misread throughout; the transcript then asserts 4:3 = 24:16, which is false
numeral misread (11:7 is not triple)

tr_errors.english: Its proof will be the following 24 to 16, namely sesquitertia ... 4 to 3 is equal to 24 to 16
tr_errors.problem: the translation repeats the misread figures, so the worked example teaches false arithmetic

tr_errors.problem: the garbled ratio name is left untranslated and covered with a vague note

book_verdict: The prose is read well, but the numbers fail where the book is about numbers. Worked ratios are misread (336:28→36:15, 24:18→24:16), so the arithmetic shown is false, and the Hebrew numeral letters on the magic-square page are flattened into digits. The catalogue date 1566 is too early for a copy that cites Esch Mezareph.
